videos.script: Everything so far has been about getting things into the history. This lesson is about three kinds of thing that should not go in, or not in the ordinary way. {{three}} The first is clutter. Log files, the operating system's leftovers, other people's code that a tool downloads. A file called gitignore lists them, and Git stops mentioning them. {{ignore}} The second is secrets. A password committed by mistake does not leave when you delete the file. It stays in the history, in every clone, for good. The only real fix is to change the password. {{secret}} And the third is big files. Git keeps every version of every file, which is wonderful for text and expensive for photos and videos. Ten versions of a large photo are ten large photos, in every copy. {{big}} Git LFS stores them somewhere else and keeps a small note in their place. {{lfs}} And one more thing that is not quite a file: another project inside yours, pinned to one exact commit. That is a submodule. {{title}}
